newsitem.title: UK: AXA-UAP to sell UK insurer - paper.
newsitem.headline: AXA-UAP to sell UK insurer - paper.

text.p: French insurance combine Axa and Union des Assurances de Paris, which recently announced the formation of a partnership called AXA-UAP, plans to rationalise its UK holdings by selling off one of its British insurers, The Times reported on Monday.
The report said the insurer will sell Equity and Law, a UK insurance firm in an auction which could raise up to one billion stg -- double the 467 million price tag paid by AXA in 1987.

The Times added that AXA-UAP also holds a 60 percent stake in the UK Sun Life Group which includes the general insurer, Provincial. A sell-off of that stake is cited as another possibility in the report, which does not name any sources.

Demand for UK insurers is seen as high, with a race already under way to take over the mutual insurer Scottish Amicable which has seen five suitors come forward. National Westminster Bank was also reported to have come forward at the last minute, according to weekend press reports.
